card.name: Linking word after a stated effect
card.fires_on: The word 'when', 'result', or a comma right after a clause that states an effect or condition, where the text goes on to give the circumstance or outcome. Mostly in drug-label warnings.

modes.label: 'when' after an effect
modes.description: 'when' follows a clause about impaired response or status and introduces the circumstance.
modes.example: Patients taking thiazides or loop diuretics may have impaired response to these therapies<< when>> taking NSAIDs.

modes.label: 'result' after 'may'
modes.description: The verb 'result' follows 'may' and leads into a list of outcomes.
modes.example: Air embolism may<< result>> in stroke, organ ischemia and/or

modes.label: Comma after a condition
modes.description: A comma ends a conditional clause and the consequence follows.

card.writes: It pushes toward words that continue with a consequence or circumstance, and away from words about need.
card.plain: It marks the spot where a sentence turns from a condition to its consequence or circumstance.
